amanecer.resumen: At the Moon's south pole the Sun barely sets. Two astronauts, 7 days: air is made from water and energy, and recovering water also costs energy.

nebula.briefing: Air needs energy: oxygen is made by splitting water. And recovering water costs energy too. Here the Sun doesn't set for the whole mission.
nebula.construir: Watch the mass bar: every kilo you put on the rocket counts. The recycler is heavy, but it recovers almost all the water.
nebula.exito: Mission complete! Now we travel to Mars. Your reserves come with you.

noche.resumen: First stop: the Moon. Four astronauts, 30 days. After a few days the Sun sets and the lunar night arrives: almost 15 days without light. Keep the air running until dawn.

nebula.briefing: Hi! I'm Nebula, the expedition's pilot cat. First stop: the Moon. Soon the Sun sets and the panels produce nothing. How will you keep the air running until dawn?
nebula.construir: Hint: count how much energy your base uses per day and multiply it by the nights.
nebula.exito: You made it to dawn! Whatever you saved carries over as a reserve to the next mission. This is how NASA thinks when it designs the Fission Surface Power reactor.

eventos: The water recycler breaks down for 3 days.

tormenta.titulo: Extra · Solar storm on the Moon
tormenta.resumen: Based on the real storm of May 2024. On the rim of Shackleton crater there is almost always light, but the Sun is also a threat: four astronauts, 20 days, and a flare on the way.

nebula.briefing: NASA satellites watch the Sun. When they warn of a flare, you will have one day to react.
nebula.construir: Shielding protects every day, but it is heavy. The shelter protects a lot, but no science is done while inside.
nebula.exito: Well done! This is how Artemis astronauts will protect themselves on the Moon.

eventos: DONKI alert: solar particles detected near Earth (May 9, 2024). They will arrive in force tomorrow.
The solar particles arrive! (May 10, 2024, Kp 9 storm: the strongest in 20 years)
New burst of particles: DONKI records 6 events this day (May 13, 2024).

hielo.resumen: Forty days next to a crater in eternal shadow, where LCROSS found ice. Bringing all the water from Earth weighs too much: can you get it from the ground?

nebula.briefing: Making oxygen uses water every day. Over 40 days that is a lot of water to lift on a rocket.
nebula.construir: The extractor heats the regolith to release the ice, but it is heavy and uses energy.
nebula.exito: You used the Moon's own resources! That is called ISRU and it is key to the Artemis program.

eventos: The water recycler breaks down for 3 days.

cadena.resumen: Thirty days in the Sea of Rains. A micrometeorite, the lunar night, a solar storm and a breakdown, one after another. Design a base that can take it all.

nebula.briefing: This mission combines everything you have learned. I will not give hints during the trip.
nebula.construir: Think about the worst day: at night, with broken panels and the recycler down.
nebula.exito: A real commander! Your base survived a chain of problems, just like in a real mission.

eventos: Alert: solar flare detected. The particles will arrive tomorrow.
The water recycler breaks down for 4 days.

marte.resumen: Thirty sols in Jezero crater, where Perseverance explores. Less than half the sunlight arrives, the greenhouse needs energy and a dust storm is coming, like the one that shut down Opportunity.

nebula.briefing: We made it to Mars! New base: before you decide, check your reserves. Mars has a CO₂ atmosphere: MOXIE can turn it into oxygen without using water.
nebula.construir: Panels produce less than half of what they do on the Moon, and dust can cover them for days. More energy for the crops leaves less for later.
nebula.exito: First harvest on Mars! This harvest stays as a reserve for the next mission.

eventos: Mars satellites see a dust storm growing.
Dust storm! Only a quarter of the sunlight arrives for 10 sols.

tormenta_marte.resumen: Based on the real event of May 20, 2024, which the Curiosity rover measured on Mars. A solar alert arrives by radio, but Earth is slow to answer: this time, you make the plan.

nebula.briefing: From Mars, a signal takes between about 4 and 24 minutes to arrive from Earth. If a solar alert arrives, you can't wait for an answer: you decide when to go into the shelter.
nebula.construir: Shielding protects every day, but it is heavy. The shelter protects a lot, but no science is done while inside.
nebula.exito: You protected your crew! This is how the astronauts who reach Mars will prepare.

eventos: Message from Earth, received 12 minutes late: DONKI saw a big flare heading to Mars (May 20, 2024). The particles arrive tomorrow.
The solar particles arrive! The Curiosity rover measured the biggest radiation surge since it landed on Mars.

cero.resumen: Your first day as commander: a small base, two astronauts and six days. Learn to design, predict, advance, see the cause of a failure and fix it.

nebula.briefing: Welcome, commander! I'm Nebula. This is a training base: two astronauts, six days. In three days the Sun sets.
nebula.construir: First let's launch the base as it is, to see what happens. Making mistakes here is part of the training.
nebula.exito: Training complete! You know how to design, predict, advance and fix things with the Chronoscope. The expedition is waiting for you.
